heading: Frequently asked questions.
description: Everything you need to know before kicking the tires on Helix.

items.question: What is an "atom"?
items.answer: An atom is the smallest unit of work Helix will execute on your behalf — typically a focused, reviewable change with explicit preconditions and a single goal. Atoms compose into a build graph Helix can parallelize and verify.

items.question: Does Helix actually run code, or only plan?
items.answer: Helix plans, executes, and verifies. Atoms are executed against your repository inside an isolated environment with type-check, tests, lint, and contract assertions as gating checks.

items.question: How big are the PRs Helix produces?
items.answer: Small. Each PR corresponds to one or a handful of related atoms — typically tens to low-hundreds of lines, not thousands. You review and merge at your own pace.

items.question: Do I have to merge the PRs Helix opens?
items.answer: No. Every PR is a proposal — humans stay in the loop. You can review, request changes, or close. Helix never pushes directly to main.

items.question: Which languages and frameworks does Helix support?
items.answer: Helix is language-agnostic at the orchestration layer and ships first-class verifiers for TypeScript, Python, Go, and Rust. Custom verifiers can be added per-repository.

items.question: Is Helix open source?
items.answer: Yes. Helix is open source under the MIT license. Self-host the orchestrator or use the hosted version — same code path.
